identity.title: Second-Order Min-Max Optimization with Lazy Hessians

problem.claim: Develop second-order methods for convex-concave minimax optimization, including its strongly-convex-strongly-concave variant.

gap.claim: It remains unclear whether the stated computational complexity can be improved.

contributions.claim: A method reuses Hessians across iterations to reduce computation cost.

Assuming first-order oracle cost N and second-order oracle cost dN, the authors report Õ((N+d²)(d+d^(2/3)ε^(-2/3))) for convex-concave problems and Õ((N+d²)(d+d^(2/3)κ^(2/3))) for strongly-convex-strongly-concave problems with condition number κ.
Numerical experiments cover real and synthetic datasets.

stated_novelty.claim: The stated distinction is reducing computation by reusing Hessians across iterations, with a reported d^(1/3) improvement over previous methods.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report an overall complexity improving previous methods by a factor of d^(1/3).
For strongly-convex-strongly-concave problems, the authors report a similar speedup over the state-of-the-art method.
The authors report that numerical experiments on real and synthetic datasets verify the method's efficiency.

narrative_sequence.summary: The paper studies second-order methods for convex-concave minimax optimization.
Prior work is reported to achieve optimal iteration complexity O(ε^(-3/2)) for finding an ε-saddle point, while improvement of the associated computational complexity is unclear.
The proposed methods reduce computation by reusing Hessians across iterations.
The abstract reports a d^(1/3) speedup, an extension to strongly-convex-strongly-concave problems, and supporting numerical experiments.

source_observation.claim: The abstract explicitly separates iteration complexity from oracle-based computational complexity and states the oracle-cost assumptions used.

lessons.interpretation: This framing makes the computational bottleneck and the basis of the comparison explicit.
lessons.application: When presenting an optimization method, define the cost model and report iteration and total computational complexity separately.
lessons.exception: This separation may be unnecessary when all oracle calls have essentially identical, fixed cost.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the exact previous methods or baselines underlying the reported speedups.
The numerical datasets, metrics, implementation details, and experimental conditions are not provided.
The meaning and hidden factors in the Õ bounds are unspecified.
